explain.say: Soil starts as solid rock, called bedrock. Frost, rain, heat and plant roots slowly crack and break it into smaller and smaller pieces. This is weathering.

faq.a: Soil forms when rock is broken down by weathering and mixed with humus, the rotted remains of plants and animals, plus air and water. Living things like worms and microbes help mix and build it.
Humus is the dark, crumbly material made when worms, fungi and bacteria break down dead leaves, roots and animals. It holds water and nutrients that plants need.

faq.q: What are the layers of soil?
faq.a: From the top: leaf litter, dark topsoil rich in humus and life, lighter subsoil with clay and minerals, broken rock, and solid bedrock at the bottom. These layers are called soil horizons.

faq.q: How long does soil take to form?
faq.a: Very slowly. In many places it takes a few hundred to a thousand years or more to make a few centimetres of new soil.
Earthworms tunnel through soil, letting in air and water, and they eat dead plants and mix them down into the soil, helping make humus.
asks: Why are worms good for soil?

facts: Making just a few centimetres of new soil can take hundreds of years or more.
A handful of healthy soil can contain billions of microbes.
